quiz.q: Who is regarded as the father of nematology?
quiz.e: N. A. Cobb established nematology as a discipline and devised the sieving-and-decanting extraction method.

quiz.q: The feeding structure that distinguishes plant-parasitic nematodes from free-living forms is the:
quiz.e: All plant-parasitic nematodes possess a protrusible stylet used to puncture cells and withdraw contents.

quiz.q: In Tylenchida the stylet is a:
quiz.e: Tylenchida have a stomatostylet with basal knobs; Dorylaimida have an odontostylet without knobs.

quiz.q: How many juvenile stages occur in the typical nematode life cycle?
quiz.e: There are four juvenile stages (J1–J4) separated by moults; in Meloidogyne and Heterodera the first moult occurs inside the egg, so J2 is the infective stage.

quiz.q: The infective stage of Meloidogyne is the:
quiz.e: The J1 moults within the egg, and the J2 hatches and invades the root just behind the tip.

quiz.q: The body cavity of nematodes is a:
quiz.e: Nematodes are pseudocoelomates — the body cavity is not fully lined with mesodermal epithelium.

quiz.q: Phasmids are present in members of the class:
quiz.e: Secernentea (= Phasmidea) possess phasmids; Adenophorea (= Aphasmidea), which includes Dorylaimida, lack them.

quiz.q: Nematodes move principally by:
o: Undulatory (sinusoidal) waves against a water film
quiz.e: Longitudinal muscles acting against the hydrostatic skeleton produce sinusoidal waves; a water film is essential for movement.

quiz.q: Root-knot of vegetables is caused by:
quiz.e: Meloidogyne incognita, M. javanica, M. arenaria and M. hapla are the four most widespread species.

quiz.q: Molya disease of wheat and barley is caused by:
quiz.e: The cereal cyst nematode Heterodera avenae causes molya, an important problem in Rajasthan and adjoining areas.

quiz.q: Ear cockle of wheat is caused by:
quiz.e: Anguina tritici forms seed galls (cockles); with Rathayibacter tritici it causes the yellow ear rot or tundu disease.

quiz.q: White tip of rice is caused by:
quiz.e: A. besseyi is seed-borne and causes chlorosis and necrosis of the leaf tip in rice.

quiz.q: Ufra disease of rice is caused by:
quiz.e: Ditylenchus angustus is an ectoparasite of the growing point causing ufra, serious in deepwater rice.

quiz.q: Spreading decline of citrus and toppling of banana are caused by:
quiz.e: Radopholus similis, the burrowing nematode, is a migratory endoparasite of roots and corms.

quiz.q: Slow decline of citrus is caused by:
quiz.e: Tylenchulus semipenetrans, the citrus nematode, is a sedentary semi-endoparasite.

quiz.q: The stem and bulb nematode is:
quiz.e: D. dipsaci attacks onion, garlic and many other hosts; the desiccation-resistant 'eelworm wool' allows long survival.

quiz.q: Root lesion nematodes belong to the genus:
quiz.e: Pratylenchus is a migratory endoparasite producing characteristic necrotic root lesions.

quiz.q: The reniform nematode is:
quiz.e: Named for the kidney-shaped mature female; a sedentary semi-endoparasite of many crops including cotton and pulses.

quiz.q: Pine wilt disease is caused by:
quiz.e: The pine wood nematode is vectored by longhorn beetles of the genus Monochamus.

quiz.q: The potato cyst nematodes are:
quiz.e: Globodera species form spherical cysts; in India they are restricted mainly to the Nilgiri hills and are of quarantine importance.

quiz.q: False root-knot nematode is:
quiz.e: Nacobbus aberrans produces galls resembling root-knot but differs in biology and female morphology.

quiz.q: Which cyst nematode is important on pigeonpea?
quiz.e: Heterodera cajani is the pigeonpea cyst nematode; H. glycines is on soybean and H. schachtii on sugar beet.

quiz.q: Meloidogyne induces which feeding structure in host roots?
quiz.e: Meloidogyne induces multinucleate giant cells (usually 5–7) by repeated mitosis without cytokinesis; Heterodera induces a syncytium by cell-wall dissolution.

quiz.q: Xiphinema, Longidorus and Trichodorus are examples of:
quiz.e: These are migratory ectoparasites that feed from outside the root; several are virus vectors.

quiz.q: Which nematode is a sedentary endoparasite?
quiz.e: Meloidogyne females become sedentary and swollen inside the root; Pratylenchus is migratory endoparasitic.

quiz.q: Nepoviruses such as grapevine fanleaf virus are transmitted by:
quiz.e: Xiphinema (dagger nematodes) transmit nepoviruses; Trichodorus and Paratrichodorus (stubby-root) transmit tobraviruses such as tobacco rattle virus.

quiz.q: Hatching of potato cyst nematode eggs is chiefly stimulated by:
quiz.e: Root diffusates (hatching factors) from potato and other solanaceous hosts trigger emergence of J2 from eggs within the cyst.

quiz.q: The Mi gene in tomato confers resistance to root-knot nematode but breaks down above about:
quiz.e: Mi-mediated resistance is heat-labile and is generally lost above roughly 28 °C.

quiz.q: A disease complex commonly reported between root-knot nematode and which fungus?
quiz.e: Meloidogyne predisposes roots to Fusarium wilt, and the complex breaks wilt resistance in several crops.

quiz.q: Cobb's sieving and decanting technique separates nematodes on the basis of:
quiz.e: Soil particles settle faster than nematodes, so decanting through graded sieves concentrates the nematodes.

quiz.q: The Baermann funnel technique recovers:
quiz.e: Only nematodes able to migrate through the tissue paper are collected, so eggs and inactive stages are missed.

quiz.q: Cysts are separated from soil most efficiently using:
quiz.e: The Fenwick can floats cysts off dried soil; the Seinhorst elutriator and mist chamber serve other extraction purposes.

quiz.q: Meloidogyne species are classically identified from the:
o: Stylet knob shape of the male only
quiz.e: The perineal pattern — cuticular striae around the vulva and anus of the mature female — is the classical character, now supported by esterase phenotypes and molecular markers.

quiz.q: Egg masses of root-knot nematode on roots are stained with:
quiz.e: Phloxine B (0.015%) stains egg masses pink for counting; acid fuchsin stains nematodes inside root tissue.

quiz.q: Nematodes are killed and fixed for permanent mounts using:
quiz.e: Gentle heat killing straightens the specimens; FA 4:1 (formalin–acetic acid) is a standard fixative.

quiz.q: In the gall index scale of 0–5, a score of 5 indicates:
quiz.e: The common scale is 0 = none, 1 = 1–2, 2 = 3–10, 3 = 11–30, 4 = 31–100 and 5 = more than 100 galls per root system.

quiz.q: Nematode population densities in soil are conventionally expressed per:
quiz.e: Counts are commonly reported per 200 g (or per kg) of oven-dry soil; the basis must always be stated.

quiz.q: Which is a systemic granular nematicide?
quiz.e: Carbofuran and phorate are granular carbamate/organophosphate nematicides; the others are fumigants.

quiz.q: Pasteuria penetrans used in nematode management is a:
quiz.e: Pasteuria penetrans is an obligate bacterial parasite whose endospores attach to the cuticle of juveniles.

quiz.q: Purpureocillium lilacinum (formerly Paecilomyces lilacinus) mainly parasitises:
quiz.e: It is an egg-parasitic fungus; Pochonia chlamydosporia (formerly Verticillium chlamydosporium) acts similarly on eggs and females.

quiz.q: Marigold (Tagetes) suppresses nematodes because it contains:
quiz.e: Alpha-terthienyl and related thiophenes are nematicidal; marigold is used as a trap or antagonistic crop.

quiz.q: Soil solarization controls nematodes principally by:
o: Raising soil temperature under transparent polythene
quiz.e: Moist soil mulched with transparent polythene in summer heats the upper layers enough to kill many propagules.

quiz.q: Which is the most appropriate cultural measure against a sedentary endoparasite with a wide host range?
o: Crop rotation with non-hosts and summer ploughing
quiz.e: Rotation with poor or non-hosts, deep summer ploughing and destruction of volunteers reduce inoculum.

quiz.q: Hot water treatment of planting material is chiefly used against nematodes in:
o: Banana suckers and other vegetative planting material
quiz.e: Suckers, setts, bulbs and rhizomes are commonly treated in hot water to kill nematodes carried internally.

quiz.q: The economic threshold level for a nematode is:
o: The population at which visible symptoms first appear
The density at which control cost equals the value of damage prevented
quiz.e: Management is justified when the expected loss exceeds the cost of the control measure.

quiz.q: Neem and castor cakes reduce nematode populations mainly by:
o: Releasing toxic compounds and enhancing antagonistic soil microflora
quiz.e: Oil cakes release nematotoxic compounds on decomposition and stimulate antagonistic fungi and bacteria.

quiz.q: Mustard used as a green manure suppresses nematodes through:
quiz.e: Glucosinolates in Brassica tissue hydrolyse to isothiocyanates, the basis of biofumigation.
